basic_information.short_title: Bangsamoro Regional Hospital and Medical Center Act of 2025
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE MAGUINDANAO PROVINCIAL HOSPITAL TO BE KNOWN AS THE “BANGSAMORO REGIONAL HOSPITAL AND MEDICAL CENTER” TO A LEVEL III HOSPITAL, AND THEREBY INCREASING ITS BED CAPACITY TO THREE HUNDRED FIFTY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after complete publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Turns the Maguindanao Provincial Hospital into the Bangsamoro Regional Hospital and Medical Center — a 350-bed Level III teaching hospital, the highest classification in the region.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To give the region its own top-tier referral hospital, so patients needing trauma, stroke, cancer, dialysis or specialist surgical care are not sent outside the Bangsamoro for it.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The hospital moves from Level II to Level III with 350 beds. Level III means a teaching hospital with accredited residency training in four specialties, plus trauma and stroke care, an oncology centre, dialysis, a blood bank and interventional radiology.
who_will_be_affected: Patients across the region needing tertiary care
Residents of Maguindanao del Sur and nearby areas
Doctors in training, since Level III requires accredited residency programmes
Health workers, whose numbers must increase with the beds
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2025 — 15 days after complete publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. The region gets its own top-tier hospital: 350 beds, Level III, with cancer care, dialysis, trauma and stroke services, and doctors trained on site.
in_practice: Maguindanao Provincial Hospital at Datu Hoffer Ampatuan, Maguindanao del Sur, becomes the Bangsamoro Regional Hospital and Medical Center
Level II becomes Level III; bed capacity rises to 350
Level III requires a teaching or training hospital with accredited residency programmes in Medicine, Pediatrics, Obstetrics and Gynecology, and Surgery

It must also provide trauma and stroke care, an oncology and wellness centre, physical medicine and rehabilitation, an ambulatory surgical clinic, dialysis, a blood bank, a tertiary laboratory with histopathology, and Level III imaging with interventional radiology
Physical structures, services, facilities and equipment comprehensively upgraded, with modern infrastructure and advanced medical technologies
The workforce — doctors, nurses, other practitioners and support staff — increased accordingly, with additional plantilla positions determined by MOH with the finance ministry
₱50,000,000 initial from the 2025 Bangsamoro budget; implementing rules within 60 days

for_specific_groups.Patients needing specialist care: Cancer, dialysis, trauma, stroke and complex surgery become available inside the region rather than through referral elsewhere.
for_specific_groups.Doctors and medical graduates: Level III status requires accredited residency training in four major specialties — the region gains a teaching hospital.
for_specific_groups.Health workers: Section 7 requires the workforce to increase, with new permanent posts determined and filled.
for_specific_groups.Residents of Maguindanao del Sur: The objectives name you specifically, along with the sick, the poor and other marginalised individuals.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: Datu Hoffer Ampatuan, Maguindanao del Sur — serving the whole region as its top referral hospital.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2025; the services depend on the upgrade being delivered.
what_you_can_do: Ask the Ministry of Health for the implementing rules, due within 60 days
Ask which Level III services are operating — the act lists them in Section 4
watch_out_for: ₱50 million is the same initial figure given to 25-bed hospitals elsewhere in the registry, for a 350-bed tertiary medical centre.
No completion deadline is set and no progress report is required — unlike BAA 73, passed a week earlier.
Level III accreditation depends on meeting every service standard in Section 4, not on the act alone.

key_terms_explained.Level III hospital: The highest classification — a teaching hospital with residency training, plus trauma, stroke, oncology, dialysis, blood bank and interventional radiology.
key_terms_explained.Tertiary care: Specialist care beyond what a general hospital provides.
key_terms_explained.Plantilla positions: Permanent, funded posts in the government staffing structure.
key_terms_explained.DOH AO 2012-0012: The national administrative order setting hospital classification standards, which the act quotes at length.
key_terms_explained.Histopathology: Laboratory examination of tissue, needed for cancer diagnosis.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Dhu Al-Qa'dah 28, 1446 / 26 May 2025, approved by Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua on 9 July 2025.

everyday_scenarios: A patient needing dialysis or cancer treatment previously travelled outside the region. Level III status requires an oncology and wellness centre and a dialysis facility on site.
A stroke patient needs care within hours. Level III requires provision for trauma and stroke care.
A medical graduate from the region wants residency training close to home. Level III requires accredited residency programmes in Medicine, Pediatrics, Obstetrics and Gynecology, and Surgery.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Regional Hospital and Medical Center Act of 2025”.

Section 2 — Policy: protect and promote the people's right to health, instill health consciousness, and adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development providing essential goods, health care and other social services to all people at an affordable cost.

Section 3 — Objectives: upgrade the Maguindanao Provincial Hospital to a Level III hospital with 350-bed capacity; integrate the Universal Health Care Act; improve government health services for the general public, especially residents of Maguindanao del Sur and nearby areas; provide essential and quality health services especially to the sick, the poor and other marginalised individuals; and improve the morale and the social and economic well-being of the hospital's health workers.

Section 4 — Defines the DOH classification levels in detail. Level III requires all of Level II capacity plus a teaching and/or training hospital with an accredited residency training programme in Medicine, Pediatrics, Obstetrics and Gynecology, and Surgery; provision for trauma and stroke care; an oncology and wellness centre; a physical medicine and rehabilitation unit; an ambulatory surgical clinic; a dialysis facility; a blood bank; a DOH-licensed tertiary clinical laboratory equipped for histopathology; and a DOH-licensed Level III imaging facility with interventional radiology.

Section 5 — Upgrades the Maguindanao Provincial Hospital, located in Datu Hoffer Ampatuan, Maguindanao del Sur, from Level II to a Level III hospital with 350-bed capacity, to be known as the Bangsamoro Regional Hospital and Medical Center, in accordance with national classification standards of the DOH Bureau of Health Facilities and Services, to attain full accreditation.

Section 6 — Existing physical structures, professional health care services, facilities and equipment are comprehensively upgraded and expanded to accommodate the increased bed capacity, incorporating modern infrastructure, advanced medical technologies and innovative systems.

Section 7 — The existing workforce — doctors, nurses, other health care practitioners and support personnel — shall be increased accordingly. The MOH, coordinating with the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Management and the hospital management, determines the additional plantilla positions to be created and filled.
Section 8 — The hospital remains under the administrative supervision of the MOH, authorised to establish and approve the organisational structure and personnel.
Section 9 — Implementing rules to be formulated by the MOH within 60 days of promulgation.
Section 10 — An initial ₱50,000,000 is charged against the 2025 General Appropriation Act of the Bangsamoro, with funds for operations thereafter in the annual appropriations for the following year.
Section 13 — Takes effect 15 days after complete publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM.

citizen_questions.q: What does Level III mean for me?
citizen_questions.a: It is the highest hospital classification. On top of everything a Level II provides, the hospital must have accredited residency training in four specialties, trauma and stroke care, an oncology and wellness centre, physical medicine and rehabilitation, an ambulatory surgical clinic, dialysis, a blood bank, a tertiary laboratory with histopathology, and Level III imaging with interventional radiology.
350, up from its Level II capacity.
Datu Hoffer Ampatuan, Maguindanao del Sur. It becomes the region's referral hospital, renamed the Bangsamoro Regional Hospital and Medical Center.

citizen_questions.q: How much money is behind it?
citizen_questions.a: An initial ₱50 million from the 2025 Bangsamoro budget — the same initial figure given to 25-bed hospitals elsewhere in the registry. Continuing operations come through later annual appropriations.
The act sets no completion deadline. Implementing rules were due from the Ministry of Health within 60 days, and full Level III accreditation depends on meeting every standard in Section 4.
